text:
{
  "status": "NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT",
  "SYSTEM_INTERPRETATION_OF_USER_INTENT": "The system treats past interactions as continuing demand for broadly related items, with insufficient attention to the specific purpose and timing of the next choice.",
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_RIGHT": [
    "Recommendations align when they preserve a specific connection to prior interests, such as a musical style, artist, narrative mood, or practical task.",
    "Complementary supplies and upgrades appeal when they support existing equipment or add a clearly useful capability."
  ],
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_WRONG": [
    "Broadly related products compete with closer matches despite lacking the compatibility, function, tone, or musical qualities users seek.",
    "Historical interests are treated as current needs even when recent purchases already satisfy them or recent behavior suggests a different priority.",
    "Several substitutes or overlapping products are treated as independent purchase opportunities, although users usually want one suitable option."
  ],
  "OVERUSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Shared category, brand ecosystem, material, or broad genre substitutes for a specific reason to choose an item.",
    "An isolated past interaction is extended into continuing demand for related devices, accessories, seasonal content, or replacement products."
  ],
  "UNDERUSED_OR_MISSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Exact compatibility, intended task, dimensions, connector type, and ownership determine whether practical products are useful.",
    "Recent behavior and already satisfied needs affect whether a related item adds value now.",
    "Fine distinctions in entertainment mood, style, performer, and repertoire determine preference within broad categories.",
    "Unidentifiable items generate uncertainty rather than evidence of dislike, limiting what feedback can establish about their relevance."
  ],
  "PRIMARY_FAILURE_MODE_AT_TOP_OF_LIST": "The top ranks contain broadly plausible associations that lack a specific current reason to choose them, reducing the number of distinct, immediately useful matches.",
  "DIAGNOSTIC_SIGNALS_TO_TRACK": [
    "Track the share of top-ranked recommendations users would choose now, distinguishing immediate choices from general interest and uncertainty.",
    "Track rejection reasons involving incompatible specifications, unsupported tasks, already satisfied needs, or mismatched entertainment mood.",
    "Track how often direct task or taste matches rank below items connected only by category or brand.",
    "Track how often multiple top-ranked items satisfy the same need while users indicate they would choose only one."
  ]
}
